correctness.rationale: The entrance-law normalization agrees with the symmetric Itô convention in Kou. Mapping the excursion process gives the stated time-position intensity; at x>0 the joint density of the winning point is that intensity multiplied by the void probability above x. The void factor cancels in the regular conditional mark law, and integrating in birth time yields the erfc ratio exactly. The centering exists uniquely for t>pi/2 since A(0)=1/sqrt(pi) and A decreases to zero. With q=u+z/(2u) the density Jacobian has prefactor rho sqrt(2t) q/(2 sqrt(pi) u^3); A(u) is asymptotic to exp(-u^2)/(2 sqrt(pi) u^2), and the excess exponent is z+r+o(1) on bounded sets. The side r=0 has zero intensity and does not affect vague convergence. The integrated intensity above z0 with r>R tends to rho exp(-z0-R); with R=0 this controls high positions and supplies the Poisson count bound for every fixed rank. These bounds, not vague convergence alone, justify ranking. Product intensity gives independent marks and u^2/log t tends to 1/2. Finite diagnostic output (104 checks) and checker were inspected, not rerun; the analytic proof establishes the limit.

value.rationale: The marginal extreme height cannot answer which founding excursions produced those extremes. The finite conditional kernel and logarithmically small founding-time scale, with independent rank marks, resolve this for the natural excursion model; in particular the winners are nearly as old as the entire process. This is a joint localization result rather than a recomputation of the known Gumbel marginal.
